settings.heading: What usually goes wrong with app projects
settings.subcopy: None of these are engineering problems. All of them are expensive.

settings.pain: We built everything, then found out nobody wanted it.
settings.answer: Prototype and test the core flow with real users before the build budget gets committed.

settings.pain: The app works but the store rejected it.
settings.answer: Review guidelines are part of the definition phase, not a surprise at submission.

settings.pain: Every change needs the original developer.
settings.answer: Documented architecture, tests and a handover session. You own the code and can leave.

settings.pain: It launched and then nothing happened.
settings.answer: Launch is a sequence, store optimisation, install campaigns, onboarding and retention, planned before release.

settings.heading: Native where it matters, cross-platform where it makes sense
settings.subcopy: Swift/SwiftUI, Kotlin/Compose, or React Native, picked from requirements, not fashion.

settings.title: Native iOS
settings.copy: Swift and SwiftUI when performance, hardware access or platform feel decide the outcome.

settings.title: Native Android
settings.copy: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, built to the same standard as the iOS side.

settings.title: React Native
settings.copy: One codebase across both platforms when the app is content and workflow rather than hardware.

settings.title: Backend & APIs
settings.copy: Auth, sync, push, offline handling and the API the app talks to, built by the same team.

settings.title: Design & prototyping
settings.copy: Flows and a clickable prototype your users can try before a line of app code exists.

settings.title: Release & ops
settings.copy: Store submission, staged rollout, crash reporting and the update cadence after launch.
